correctness.rationale: For a diagonal quadratic the published update reduces exactly to a scalar multiplicative recurrence. The source proves convergence of iterates for smooth convex objectives and square-summability of successive gradient differences, which makes each metric coordinate converge. If an active limiting metric were at most half of the base step times curvature, every multiplier would have magnitude at least one, contradicting convergence to zero. The asymptotic ratio and eventual Q-linear bound then follow by a finite-coordinate maximum argument.

value.rationale: The primary paper emphasizes robustness to arbitrary base stepsizes but supplies only a generic smooth-convex ergodic rate and iterate convergence. On the canonical separable strongly convex quadratic class, the finding identifies the exact classical instability boundary that the adaptive denominator must cross and upgrades the generic conclusion to eventual last-iterate Q-linear convergence. This directly explains a central advertised behavior of the new method rather than computing an arbitrary invariant.
